prerequisites: Knowledge of differential and integral calculus of single-variable functions

learning_outcomes.text: To pose and calculate integrals of functions of two and three variables and apply them to solving engineering problems.
To fluently parameterize curves and surfaces, perform integration of scalar and vector functions over them, and apply it to solving engineering problems.

To understand the essential qualitative aspects of differential equations: existence, uniqueness, and regularity of solutions. To acquire proficiency in the explicit resolution of first-order and higher-order differential equations, relating the latter to first-order systems.
To calculate Fourier series associated with elementary functions and solve one-dimensional heat and wave problems using the method of separation of variables.
To state and apply the basic properties of complex functions, represent them through series expansions, and calculate and classify their singularities.
To understand the concept of partial differential equations and identify some examples in Industrial Engineering where they are applied.

syllabus_topics: 1.1.3. Change of variables in double integrals
1.2.3. Change of variables in triple integrals
1.3: Applications of Double and Triple Integrals.
2.1.4. Divergence and Curl of a vector field
2.2: Line and Surface Integrals. Vector Field Theory.
2.3: Applications of Line and Surface Integrals.
3.3.1. Definition of the Laplace Transform. Properties
3.3.2. Definition of the Inverse Laplace Transform. Properties
3.3.3. Application to the resolution of differential equations
3.3.4. Application to the resolution of systems of differential equations
Theme 4: Fourier Series. Partial Differential Equations
4.1.5. Fourier series of a non-periodic function
4.2.6. Resolution of equations of Mathematical Physics
5.4: Residues and their use in Integration.
teaching_methods: Expositive classes (explanation of concepts and problem-solving examples)
Laboratory practices (computer room, software for calculations)

assessment_methods.method: Theoretical part (continuous assessment: two written tests)
Individual and/or group activities, work and class attendance

assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, the final grade is calculated as: Final = Theory × 0.70 + Practices × 0.20 + Activities × 0.10. The theoretical part involves two continuous assessment tests (Themes 1 & 2, and Themes 3, 4 & 5), each graded out of 10 and compensable from 3 points. A final exam is also available; if a student takes a part of the final exam, they waive the score from the corresponding previous continuous assessment test (if any). For extraordinary calls, the student's grade will be the maximum of (Final = Theory × 0.80 + (Practices obtained during the course) × 0.20) or (Final = Theory × 1.00). In all calls, a minimum of 4 points in the theory grade is required to pass the course; otherwise, the final grade will be 4 (Fail).
